scope: Implement the original complete-input contract's explicitly allowed, capability-checked batch path; same authenticated source, fixed2024 domain, native validators and budget
caveat: Provider warns batching can be less reliable than single calls. This is a small bounded batch capability check, not an assumed reliability improvement. IDs may be out of order and HTTP200 may contain per-item errors.
fixed_control: One batch of original first receipt, its block and historical reserve;3 methods/66CU. Compare the full boundary with the passed single-request control before any bulk.
bulk: At most10 methods/260CU per serial HTTP POST, at least1s between starts; each method counted individually including failures, no retry or provider switch. TLS verified, connection15s per named correction, total30s, response8MiB. Metadata records phase timings but no key.
identity: Require exact integer ID set, complete response count, no per-item error/null, native payload and dependency validation before marking a batch valid; no partial batch admission.
checkpoint: First100 native methods then full remainder only after checkpoint passes. Structural UNKNOWN kept as null; technical absence/mismatch blocks rather than becoming abstention.
resource_bounds: Same original8active-hours/48wall-hours/10000operations/2GiB. Prior4h/300operation reservations unchanged; current phase ends2026-10-13T11:25:50Z. Three new control methods and two additional documentation reads charged. No quota or billing changes.
budget_projection: Approximately563POSTs for5628 remaining native methods, before controls. Request/byte/time budget fit checked before and throughout. This is not a guarantee of actual monthly quota or completion.
failure_exit: First new transport/native validation failure pauses dependencies, diagnosis before any retry. All prior failures and binding snapshots remain immutable.
